items.markdown:
Thailand’s retirement visas (officially Non-Immigrant O or O-A visas) are `available to foreigners aged 50 and older` . To qualify, you must show proof of either ฿800,000 (approx. $22,000 USD) in a Thai bank account or a monthly income/pension of ฿65,000 (approx. $1,800 USD). Visas are valid for one year and are renewable.[](https://www.banyangroupresidences.com/news/thailand-retirement-visa-guide) [[1]](https://www.banyangroupresidences.com/news/thailand-retirement-visa-guide)[[2]](https://thailandelitevisa.com/thailand-retirement-visa-complete-guide/)

The main retirement visa pathways vary in duration, financial requirements, and mandatory insurance:[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5mUBLP1e1_A&t=420) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5mUBLP1e1_A&t=420)[[2]](https://rumavi.com/en/property-guides/thailand-retirement-visa)

1. Standard Retirement Visa (Non-Immigrant O / O-A)

- **Duration:** 1 year, renewable annually.[](https://www.banyangroupresidences.com/news/thailand-retirement-visa-guide) 
- **Financial Requirements:** Either an ฿800,000 balance in a Thai bank account (seasoned for at least 2–3 months prior to applying) or a monthly income of at least ฿65,000. A combination of both is also accepted.[](https://www.banyangroupresidences.com/news/thailand-retirement-visa-guide) 
- **Insurance:** Mandatory health insurance is required for O-A visas applied from your home country, generally covering ฿400,000 for inpatient and ฿40,000 for outpatient care.[](https://thailandelitevisa.com/thailand-retirement-visa-complete-guide/) 
- **Process:** Apply via the [Thailand e-Visa Official Portal](https://www.thaievisa.go.th/visa/retirement) or through an in-country immigration office if you entered on an initial tourist or Non-O visa.[](https://www.banyangroupresidences.com/news/thailand-retirement-visa-guide) [[1]](https://www.thaievisa.go.th/visa/retirement)

2. Long Stay Visa (Non-Immigrant O-X)

- **Duration:** Up to 10 years (issued in 5-year blocks).
- **Financial Requirements:** Requires ฿3 million deposited in a Thai bank account (must remain in the account at a minimum of ฿1.5 million) OR ฿1.8 million in the bank plus a yearly income of ฿1.2 million.
- **Eligibility:** Limited to citizens of specific countries (including the US, UK, Australia, and Germany).[](https://www.banyangroupresidences.com/news/thailand-retirement-visa-guide) 

3. Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa – Wealthy Pensioner

- **Duration:** 10 years (renewable).
- **Requirements:** Specifically for retirees with a passive income of at least $80,000 USD per year. (If your income is between $40,000 and $80,000, you must invest an additional $400,000 USD in Thai government bonds or property).
- **Benefits:** Includes fast-track immigration and exemption from the standard 90-day reporting. Apply via the [Thailand BOI LTR Visa Portal](https://ltr.boi.go.th/).[[1]](https://ltr.boi.go.th/)[[2]](https://www.issacompass.com/insights/best-retirement-visas-for-thailand-which-option-is-right-for-you)

Ongoing Responsibilities

- **90-Day Reporting:** For standard visas, you must notify the Immigration Bureau of your current address every 90 days, which can be done easily via the official [Thai Immigration](https://www.immigration.go.th/) website.
- **Re-Entry Permits:** You must secure a re-entry permit prior to leaving the country if you wish to maintain your visa's validity.[](https://www.banyangroupresidences.com/news/thailand-retirement-visa-guide) 

*Note: For official, localized requirements and forms in your specific country, it is highly recommended to consult your nearest [Royal Thai Embassy](https://hague.thaiembassy.org/th/page/76475-non-immigrant-visa-o-a-%28long-stay%29) *.[[1]](https://hague.thaiembassy.org/th/page/76475-non-immigrant-visa-o-a-%28long-stay%29)
